name: Sorra staking withdraw() pays full rewards on every call
summary: sorraStaking.withdraw paid getPendingRewards, a fixed percentage of every matured deposit, on each call without recording that the rewards were paid. After its tier-0 deposit of 122,869 SOR matured, the attacker called withdraw(1) hundreds of times per transaction, collecting the 5% reward each time, emptied the contract's SOR (stakers' deposits and the 10M reward reserve) in four transactions and sold it into the SOR/WETH pair.
notes: SOR's only market was the SOR/WETH pair the attacker sold into in each transaction, so the SOR is valued at what those sales realised (rule 12): 12.8132 ETH ($46,146 at block-time WETH) left the pair across the four transactions, scaled by the share of the sold SOR that was victims' (the attacker's own 122,869 SOR deposit excluded).
Non-upgradeable, and no owner call (setTierReward, setVaultExtension, setPoolCap) occurred between deployment and the exploit; no withdraw preceded the anchor.
